data.rationale: This commit fixes a bug in PostgreSQL's join planner where join_is_legal() failed to reject illegal join orders containing invalid lateral references. When a join depends on lateral references, join_is_legal() checks that referenced relations can still be joined from the outside, but it previously overlooked lateral references traversing outer joins or relations inside sub-joinlists (e.g. when from_collapse_limit prevents flattening). To reach the modified code in join_is_legal() and make_rel_from_joinlist(), the grammar fragment adds chained LATERAL queries in multi-relation FROM clauses alongside controls for from_collapse_limit and join_collapse_limit.
seeds:
EXPLAIN (COSTS OFF)
SELECT 1 FROM t1 LEFT JOIN t2 ON true,
  LATERAL (SELECT t2.c0 OFFSET 0) s1 LEFT JOIN t3 ON s1.c0 = t3.c0,
  LATERAL (SELECT t3.c0 OFFSET 0) s2
WHERE s2.c0 > t1.c0;
